item.title: Kula Shaker Reflect on a Career Following Sanskrit
item.description: British psychedelic rockers Kula Shaker discuss their lengthy career and a stunning new album that reminds us of rock music's power.

item.title: The Olympians Instrumentally Search for a Revival
item.description: The Olympians' In Search of a Revival may be an odd album, but it's not an unfriendly one. The dozen instrumental tracks offer friendly vibes.

item.title: Ratboys Find New Clarity in Old Ghosts on New LP
item.description: Singin' to an Open Chair is a wonderful album that shows Ratboys revving their engine once again, ready to take another long, curious lap around the block.

item.title: Visions of Change Played ’80s Hardcore Punk with a ’60s Twist
item.description: The Depraved did something unusual after two albums: expanded their sound to include more overt 1960s influences, and changed their name to Visions of Change.

item.title: Da Cruz Revolutionize the Dancefloor on ‘Som Sistema’
item.description: The combination of African, South American, and Caribbean pop styles, timely themes, and impeccable club vibes make Da Cruz's new album the best yet.

item.title: Vibes Phenom Joel Ross Dips His Jazz Into Gospel Music
item.description: Joel Ross takes his usual pyrotechnics and funnels them into a refined ensemble sound that also channels sincere, powerful jazz with a gospel center.

item.title: ‘The Huntress’ Tracks the Desire for Vengeance
item.description: The Huntress casts aside simplified ideas about revenge and observes different ways to respond to a culture of misogynistic violence.

item.title: Wes Craven’s Artfully Dreadful Voice of Horror
item.description: In Wes Craven's horror films, the victim is linguistically trapped before being physically pursued – conversation itself becomes the killing ground.

item.title: Jill Scott’s New Music Is As Vibrant As Ever
item.description: Jill Scott's new album fits seamlessly with pop's retro-futuristic fascination with the 1980s. Her signature mix of poetry, hip-hop, jazz, and soul is as vibrant as ever.

item.title: MetalMatters: Best Metal Albums of January 2026
item.description: In January's best metal, Ulver return to their deep electronica, the Ruins of Beverast show off their extreme black/doom, and Zu join free-jazz madness with ambient bliss.
